subject: Analytic result for hierarchical model with non-negative parameters

messages.author: 1fe638ac9008754d
messages.subject: Analytic result for hierarchical model with non-negative parameters
parts:
Hi,

I am doing some work in statistical genomics, where computational speed is of the essence. As such, I was wondering whether anyone can think of any results/tricks to get analytic results for a hierarchical model of the form,

X ~ normal(beta_1 z_1 + beta_2 z_2 + ... + beta_p z_p, sigma)
beta_i ~ unspecified distribution(beta_top), where I=1,...,p,

such that the individual beta_i are all non-negative?

Note: I know I could use sampling, numerical integration, etc. to achieve this result, but am really in need of analytic results due to the scale of the problem at hand.

I suspect the answer is 'no' to the above, but thought I'd ask in case anyone has any bright ideas.

Best,

Ben

It's really hard to get analytic results for unspecified distributions. Are you asking whether there are distributions you can choose to make it analytic? If so, exponential families all the way down.

But really, no one (including yourself) can help you without fully specifying your problem.

Note: I know I could use sampling, numerical integration, etc. to achieve this result, but am really in need of analytic results due to the scale of the problem at hand.

I suspect the answer is 'no' to the above, but thought I'd ask in case anyone has any bright ideas.

Good luck. 

Best,

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Analytic result for hierarchical model with non-negative parameters
parts:
Hi Dan,

Thanks for your answer. The reason I haven't specified a distribution for the prior is that I am open to any choices that yield non-negative parameters! So I would happily specify the unspecified distribution as a log-normal, gamma, weibull etc for the prior, so long as the resultant model had quantities that could be derived analytically. Hope that makes sense?

Conjugate priors won't work here because of non-negativity constraints.

Best,

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Analytic result for hierarchical model with non-negative parameters
parts:
On Monday, December 12, 2016 at 3:45:57 PM UTC-5, Ben Lambert wrote:
I am doing some work in statistical genomics, where computational speed is of the essence.
How fast do you need it for what number of observations and predictors?

As such, I was wondering whether anyone can think of any results/tricks to get analytic results for a hierarchical model of the form,

X ~ normal(beta_1 z_1 + beta_2 z_2 + ... + beta_p z_p, sigma)
beta_i ~ unspecified distribution(beta_top), where I=1,...,p,

such that the individual beta_i are all non-negative?

I'm pretty sure there is no known analytical solution. But there are tricks to evaluate the likelihood with O(p^2) complexity. For the prior I would tend to make beta the product of a simplex and an unknown scaled parameter.

Ben

messages.author: 1fe638ac9008754d
messages.subject: Re: Analytic result for hierarchical model with non-negative parameters
parts:
Hi Ben,

Thanks for your response. So the LHS is univariate (it measures phenotypes across N ~ 10,000 individuals), and the predictors are something like genotypes for individual SNPs (not exactly so because these variables can only have non-negative effects on the phenotypes). Because of the univariate nature of the LHS, evaluating the likelihood shouldn't be too problematic, since there is no need to invert a big matrix. However the computational issues appear because this model is being refit across 100,000s of individual "SNPs" in a sort of GWAS context.

As such, I was hoping to avoid having to do sampling for each of the models. I could try variational Bayes, but before I did so I wanted to see whether anything already existed out there! As I said, I expect this isn't the case but wanted to check to make sure.

Best,

Ben
